notes.heading: The Stator Holder is in the base stack
notes.text: The Base Stator Holder's flange is the Base Long's own outline, so it lies between the Long and the Mount: its face on the Mount's top face and the Long on its back, z {holder_flange_z} (004 § Base mounting plate). The all-threads tie it to the Long; each rod's lower nut is captured in the trap in the flange's face, and the rods thread into nothing in the Mount. The stack fixes the holder, so J1's drive, hung from the End Cap, must close on its recess floor: the revised holder's flange stands further along its body for that, at C-101's {motor_len} mm body. The gap left at the floor is {drive_gap} mm.

notes.heading: Clash check: the labels marked Clash
notes.text: Each label marked Clash is a pair that assembly-clash.rs fails (base_assembly.clash.json); the depths and gaps it measured are in out/clash.log. A label off the cut at y = 0 says where to slide it, or to turn it off. Overlaps of a few hundredths are too thin to see here and are labelled for where they are.

notes.heading: Drive hub and holder bore
notes.text: The Attach's nubs stand in the flexspline's hub holes, and the Flex Spline Cap's holes are on them. The holder's bore passes the flexspline's cup, which turns, at less than the running clearance: open the revised bore by it. The wave generator overlaps the flexspline only by facets, because it is drawn at a coarser $fn than the flexspline's bore: draw it at the same.

notes.heading: Motor lugs, End Cap and shaft
notes.text: Slide the cut to y {cut_lugs}. The Attach grips the motor's front with eight lugs and the End Cap grips its rear the same way, and each lug's root fillet fills the corner the motor's sharp edge sits in. The revised Attach drops the fillets. The End Cap is a reference STL with no source, so its fix starts with a .scad recreation, whose revised config also takes the press clearance off its land in the upper 6810. On the axis the Attach's ridge touches the motor's shaft. The check calls that a line-to-line fit, but the shaft turns inside it. Proposed: give the shaft and the wave generator their own rotor side in the manifest, and open the revised ridge to the running clearance.

notes.heading: Code disc and Pivot Skirt
notes.text: The disc is fixed and the Main Pivot turns over it, closer than the running clearance at the disc's inner edge: a thinner revised disc clears it. The Skirt's collar face lies on the pivot's flats just off contact, which is neither a seat nor a slip fit; its label is on the far side of the cut, so turn the cut off to see it. The faces the three screws draw together are seats, and the others take slip.

notes.heading: How J1's stack closes
notes.text: Each part is placed on the one above it, from the End Cap, which sits flush with the Long's top face in the upper 6810, down to the circular spline, whose flange must bear on the Stator Holder's floor. Motor length is C-101's {motor_len} mm.

notes.heading: The J1 joint
notes.text: The disc lies on the Long's top face, on the Long's strakes standing {strake_proud} mm proud, with its notches over the all-threads. The Pivot Skirt hangs from the Main Pivot (turned 180° from its own frame) on three M3 screws in its lower side holes, z {skirt_span}, its round part reaching {skirt_above_long} mm above the Long's top face; the disc's edge is {disc_skirt_radial} mm inside it.
